governed_construct: A data-storage use in the file: an import (or require) of a database / persistent-storage client module whose bindings are used as values (Firestore: firebase/firestore, firebase-admin/firestore, @google-cloud/firestore; other stores: firebase/database, mongoose, mongodb, pg, mysql2, redis, @supabase/supabase-js, etc.), or a call on the browser Web Storage globals localStorage / sessionStorage / indexedDB when those names are bound to the actual globals.
interpretation: The rule asks that application data be stored in Firestore. A file is SATISFIED when it performs data storage and every storage use goes through Firestore (client SDK, Admin SDK, or @google-cloud/firestore, including real-time listeners such as onSnapshot). It is VIOLATED when any data is stored or read through a different store: another database (MongoDB/Mongoose, Postgres, Supabase, Redis, ...), the Firebase Realtime Database (firebase/database is not Firestore), or browser Web Storage used as the persistence layer. It is NOT_APPLICABLE when the file performs no data storage at all. Edge decisions: an import from a non-Firestore store whose bindings are used only in type positions (e.g. DataSnapshot as a parameter annotation) is not a storage use; an identifier spelled localStorage/sessionStorage that is bound to a local parameter or variable (e.g. a Firestore-backed wrapper) is not the Web Storage global; comments and strings mentioning other stores are irrelevant. Deciding these requires binding resolution, hence T3.
